title: Tutoring Center Story Sprint Pack - Upper Sprint Lane

sprints.title: Greenhouse Gear Garden Voice Check
sprints.sessionFit: 10-minute tutoring warmup for one writer or a quiet pair before a short draft.
sprints.tutorSetup: Set out the page, a pencil, and two detail cards; invite the writer to choose one machine and one plant detail.
sprints.kidDirection: Write as the greenhouse helper who notices how the gears sound, move, and change the plant plan.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask which word makes the helper sound careful, curious, or excited.

pageSections.heading: Voice Detail
lines: The greenhouse helper sounds like ____________________.
The gear detail that fits this voice is ____________________.
One plant detail the helper notices is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Sentence Shape
lines: A short starter sentence could be ____________________.
A longer detail sentence could add ____________________.
The two sentences connect when ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Ending Beat
lines: The helper changes the gear plan by ____________________.
The final word that matches the voice is ____________________.
My greenhouse ending line is ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: One voice word I used well was ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Next time, I can add one sharper machine detail: ____________________.

sprints.title: Index Card Theater Dialogue Turn
sprints.sessionFit: 12-minute tutoring sprint for shaping a tiny scene with a clear shift.
sprints.tutorSetup: Place three index cards face down, then have the writer pick one setting card and one voice card.
sprints.kidDirection: Create a two-line exchange where the second line changes what the scene is about.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask what the speaker wants before the line and what changes after the reply.

pageSections.heading: Scene Voice
lines: The first speaker sounds ____________________.
The second speaker sounds ____________________.
The theater setting creates a mood of ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Dialogue Turn
lines: The first line of dialogue is ____________________.
The reply changes the plan because ____________________.
A stage action between the lines is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Paragraph Finish
lines: The paragraph begins with ____________________.
The middle sentence should reveal ____________________.
My theater ending line is ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: The line that changed my scene most was ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Add one stage action that shows voice: ____________________.

sprints.title: Margin Note Market Revision Choice
sprints.sprintSkill: specific revision choice from a margin note
sprints.sessionFit: 10-minute tutoring warmup for turning vague feedback into one useful edit.
sprints.tutorSetup: Offer three sample margin notes and ask the writer to choose one note to make more specific.
sprints.kidDirection: Trade a fuzzy note for a clear revision task, then write the improved sentence.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask which exact word, detail, or order change will help a reader follow the idea.

pageSections.heading: Market Note
lines: The fuzzy margin note says ____________________.
The clearer revision task is ____________________.
The part of the sentence to improve is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Detail Trade
lines: A plain word I can trade out is ____________________.
A stronger detail I can trade in is ____________________.
The sentence sounds clearer when ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Revised Line
lines: Before revision, the idea was ____________________.
After revision, the idea shows ____________________.
My market ending line is ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: One revision choice I can explain is ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Try the same trade on another sentence: ____________________.

sprints.title: Clue Label Tower Paragraph Label
sprints.sprintSkill: paragraph focus with clue and label details
sprints.sessionFit: 12-minute tutoring sprint for building one focused paragraph from three details.
sprints.tutorSetup: Put three object cards on the table and have the writer choose one clue worth explaining.
sprints.kidDirection: Write a museum label paragraph that tells readers what to notice first, next, and last.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask which detail belongs in the paragraph and which detail can wait.

pageSections.heading: Clue Focus
lines: The object on the tower shelf is ____________________.
The clue readers should notice first is ____________________.
A detail I can leave out for now is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Paragraph Shape
lines: My first sentence should point to ____________________.
My middle sentence should explain ____________________.
My final sentence should connect to ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Label Finish
lines: The label sounds precise when I use ____________________.
One word I can revise for focus is ____________________.
My museum ending line is ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: The detail that kept my paragraph focused was ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Write a second label with one new clue: ____________________.

sprints.title: Revision River Ferry Ending Pass
sprints.sprintSkill: ending revision with setup, turn, and final echo
sprints.sessionFit: 10-minute tutoring sprint for revising a weak ending into a clearer final beat.
sprints.tutorSetup: Ask the writer to mark one opening detail, one middle turn, and one final echo before drafting.
sprints.kidDirection: Send one rough ending across the ferry and bring back a clearer final sentence.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask what the reader should understand at the final dock.

pageSections.heading: Ferry Load
lines: The opening detail I can echo is ____________________.
The middle turn that matters is ____________________.
The rough ending currently says ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Revision Crossing
lines: One word I can cut is ____________________.
One clearer word I can add is ____________________.
The ending feels stronger because ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Final Dock
lines: The final sentence should show ____________________.
The echo from the opening is ____________________.
My ferry ending line is ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: The ending choice I improved was ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Revise one more final sentence with an echo: ____________________.

sprints.title: Compass Craft Route Paragraph
sprints.sprintSkill: paragraph route with beginning, turn, and finish
sprints.sessionFit: 12-minute tutoring sprint for planning one paragraph before drafting.
sprints.tutorSetup: Draw three small route dots and have the writer label the start, turn, and finish.
sprints.kidDirection: Plan a paragraph route, then write the sentence that moves readers through the turn.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask which sentence gives the reader the clearest direction.

pageSections.heading: Route Dots
lines: The paragraph starts at ____________________.
The paragraph turns when ____________________.
The paragraph finishes by showing ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Connection Words
lines: A word that moves the route forward is ____________________.
A phrase that explains the turn is ____________________.
A sentence that connects two route dots is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Academy Finish
lines: The clearest sentence in my route is ____________________.
One route detail I can revise is ____________________.
My compass ending line is ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: The sentence that shaped my paragraph was ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Add one more route dot for a longer paragraph: ____________________.

sprints.title: Almost Invention Instruction Voice
sprints.sprintSkill: clear instruction voice and revise-and-test ending
sprints.sessionFit: 12-minute tutoring sprint for ordering steps and ending with a useful test note.
sprints.tutorSetup: Give the writer three step cards and ask which step must come first for the invention to make sense.
sprints.kidDirection: Write a clear workshop paragraph that explains how the almost-invention gets tested and revised.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask where the reader might get confused and what sentence can fix that spot.

pageSections.heading: Step Order
lines: The invention almost works when ____________________.
The first step readers need is ____________________.
The step that needs clearer order is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Instruction Voice
lines: The instruction voice should sound ____________________.
A precise action word I can use is ____________________.
A sentence that explains the test is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Workshop Ending
lines: The test shows the inventor should revise ____________________.
The final note should help readers understand ____________________.
My invention ending line is ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: One instruction sentence I made clearer was ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Add a test note that improves the ending: ____________________.
